week1.text: By day 7 we validated 9 attack paths and closed 2, with a median of 4.5 days from validation to confirmed close and the slowest at 5. Owners acknowledged 8 tickets within 2 days across 6 teams. Of the 7 paths still open, 4 reach crown jewels and 4 sit with Network Engineering, including both VPN routes to the domain controller. The substation router path to the EMS data link waits on an OT change window scheduled for day 35, after the pilot ends. We need leadership to approve an earlier OT window for that router this week, or formally accept the risk until day 35.

week4.text: By day 28, 12 attack paths were validated and 10 were fixed and confirmed closed by a retest. 2 remain open, 2 of them reaching crown-jewel systems.
week4.model_text: By day 28 we validated 12 attack paths and confirmed 10 closed, at a median of 6.0 days and a slowest of 20 days. Across 8 owning teams, 11 tickets were acknowledged within 2 days. The 2 open paths both reach crown jewels: substation router to the EMS data link (Field Telecom, 22 days open) and corporate network to the EMS data link via the OT jump host (OT Engineering, 11 days open). Each fix, the router upgrade and RDP restriction plus MFA on the jump host, awaits an OT change window scheduled for day 35. Please hold that day 35 window firm, or approve an earlier one.
